title: Affine small-etale realization of the unbounded module derived category
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with small etale site and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For an $A$-module $M$, let $a_A(M)$ be the associated etale module sheaf, obtained by Zariski tilde followed by the canonical ringed-site extension of [def-sfb-scheme-zariski-etale-module-constructions], whose value on an affine etale $\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$ is $B\otimes_A M$. Work with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The functor $a_A$ is exact and faithful. Applied termwise it induces an equivalence
$$a_A:D(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_U),$$
where the right side is the full subcategory of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Its quasi-inverse is $R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},-)$, computed by a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every $E\in D(A)$ and integer $i$ there is a natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^i(a_A(E))\cong a_A(H^i(E))$, and $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},a_A(M))\cong M$ naturally in $M$.

source.place: Tag 071Q (lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site), composed with perfect.tex lemma-affine-compare-bounded (affine module equivalence); exactness from lemma-epsilon-flat and the affine associated-module functor.

proof.text: Put $T(M)=\widetilde M$ on the Zariski site of $U$, and $L=\epsilon_U^*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], $\widetilde M$ is quasi-coherent, so the two lemmas below apply to it. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $LT(M)$ is the quasi-coherent etale sheaf $v:V\to U\mapsto\Gamma(V,v^*\widetilde M)$. For affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] and the unit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify this value naturally with $M\otimes_A B$, or $B\otimes_A M$ by the switch $m\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes m$. The section formula sends $b\otimes m$ to $b\,v^*\tau_U(m)$, so a further affine restriction sends it to $g^\sharp(b)\otimes m$. Thus this is precisely the associated sheaf $a_A(M)$ of the statement, including its module maps. At $V=U$ the same identifications give $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},a_A(M))\cong\Gamma(U,\widetilde M)\cong M$, naturally. If $a_A(f)=a_A(g)$, applying these section identifications gives $f=g$, proving faithfulness.

By [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits], $T$ preserves finite limits. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], it also preserves all small colimits, hence finite colimits. It is therefore exact. The pullback $L$ is exact by [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison]. Since $a_A=LT$ by step 1, $a_A$ is exact as a functor to all etale module sheaves. This proves exactness in the ambient module category, rather than only in its quasi-coherent full subcategory.

For a complex $E$, exactness identifies $\ker a_A(d^i)$ with $a_A(\ker d^i)$ and $\operatorname{im}a_A(d^{i-1})$ with $a_A(\operatorname{im}d^{i-1})$. Taking the quotient gives $\mathcal H^i(a_A(E))\cong a_A(H^i(E))$. These identifications commute with complex maps because they are the kernel, image and quotient comparisons. Each resulting sheaf is quasi-coherent by step 1. The exact-functor factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives the termwise functor on the unbounded localizations. The displayed comparisons descend to natural isomorphisms there: both sides act on a roof by its two complex maps and the inverse of its quasi-isomorphism. This uses precisely the cohomology functors and localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); cohomology as kernel modulo image and localization at quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] to $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. It gives $T_D:D(A)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{Zar}})$ by termwise $T$, with inverse $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison] to the same scheme. It gives $L_D:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{Zar}})\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}})$ and identifies $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}L_D$ naturally with $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. Their composite $L_DT_D$ is the termwise functor $a_A$ of step 3, since both apply $LT$ to each term and differential. Its inverse $T_D^{-1}L_D^{-1}$ is $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{Zar}}L_D^{-1}\cong R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}L_DL_D^{-1}\cong R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}$; the last comparison is the counit of the second equivalence. Composing the units and counits of these two equivalences gives both inverse comparisons. All equivalences cited here are unbounded; no convergence assertion for a bounded-below spectral sequence is used.

On the small etale ringed site, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives a K-injective resolution $K\to I$ for every unbounded complex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to the functor on homotopy categories induced by $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},-)$ followed by localization to $D(A)$. It is exact on homotopy categories: sections is additive, so its termwise functor preserves shifts and mapping cones, whose terms use only finite direct sums. Thus $R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},K)$ is represented by the $A$-module complex $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},I)$, as claimed. The identification $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_U)=A$ is the case $M=A$ of step 1. This is the same total derived sections functor appearing in step 4, by the defining universal property of the right derived functor. Together with steps 1 and 3 this proves all remaining section and cohomology assertions.
